blockers.title: The five properties leave a shared-version release train conforming
blockers.subjectEvidence: AL-1..AL-5 contain only id and name. bundleRule forbids the aggregate bundle from being the only route by which compatible releases work, and previewRequiredPairs says only that core, TypeScript component, and control major 1 are each at N and N+1 as independently qualified bytes. No clause forbids a common version number, a shared release-train promotion predicate, or coreVersion == componentVersion as bundle-qualification policy.
blockers.governingMeasurement: At the subject-pinned file-02 digest, lines 145-147 say independent releases do not create lockstep versions and select independently qualified compatible bytes. At the subject-pinned file-04 digest, lines 182-184 say a bundle selects compatible independent releases and cannot force same-version coupling. The subject carries file 04 only from lines 191-196 and contains zero occurrences of same-version, shared version, independently versioned, or releaseIdentity.
blockers.counterexample: Publish core v1/v2 and component v1/v2 only together under one global version and promotion train; independently qualify the two byte sets; make all four runtime combinations compatible; permit direct non-bundle selection; permit independent rollback/coexistence; and keep the bundle a convenience rather than a gate. AL-1..AL-5 all pass, yet no component v3 can be published unless a core v3 is co-published. The releases remain same-version lockstep even though runtime skew works and the bundle is not the only route.
blockers.impact: The candidate's central anti-lockstep claim is weaker than both pinned governing laws and admits the exact hidden same-version gate the dispatch requires this review to attack.
blockers.requiredRepair: Bind separate core and component release identities and independent publication/promotion. Explicitly prohibit shared-version equality or bundle existence as an eligibility, qualification, or promotion predicate; make a compatible unequal-version selection prove the bundle rule; and provide a pass/fail record that distinguishes independent release from a jointly promoted train.

blockers.title: The five anti-lockstep labels do not define a conformance relation or an execution remainder
blockers.subjectEvidence: Each AL object has exactly id and name. previewRequiredPairs is one prose item, not a closed tuple set: it neither disambiguates whether fixed control major 1 or all three named items advance at N/N+1 nor enumerates the two skew directions. There are no fixture inputs, ordered rollback steps, unchanged-counterpart checks, concurrent-generation isolation observations, expected selector result, evidence object, harness identifier, or owner. DR-G16, DR-107, releaseIdentity, selectorDecision, and harness occur zero times. DR-111 appears only in the denial that this artifact does not evaluate its windows. The only execution route in the subject is CC-1..CC-11 to DR-G21.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The live DR-127 cell requires bidirectional N/N+1 skew, independent rollback/coexistence, no bundle promotion gate, and hostile dual-channel goldens. The live DR-111 row owns per-surface matrices, cross-version conformance, and the no-shared-same-version assumption; DR-107 owns multi-version generations and concurrent conflicting locks. Live DR-G16 has the aggregate-release-selection lane and signed closure evidence, whereas DR-G21's corpus is component failure containment and cannot by itself own N/N+1 publication, rollback, or coexistence. The race half therefore has detailed imported class intents and an execution route; the anti-lockstep half has neither.
blockers.counterexample: A producer can emit a JSON report with the five AL ids marked PASS, cite the single previewRequiredPairs sentence, call a whole-bundle restart 'rollback', and call two sequential installations 'coexistence'. The candidate defines no required before/after identities, no proof that the other identity stayed unchanged, no simultaneous-operation or private-closure observation, and no selector or signed evidence against which those claims fail. Conversely, an empty or self-declared support window can make AL-1/AL-2 inapplicable because 'supported' has no activation join.
blockers.impact: The artifact claims pass properties but supplies only headings. A reviewer or harness cannot reproduce a result or distinguish the row's prohibited behaviors, so the core anti-lockstep acceptance evidence remains design work rather than an execution-only remainder.
blockers.requiredRepair: Author a closed AL conformance model: separately identified/digested core and component releases; exact skew tuples and expected selection outcomes; rollback sequences proving the counterpart identity unchanged; concurrent operations proving distinct generation/private-dependency closures; and bundle/non-bundle qualification and promotion evidence. Record the DR-111 window-evaluation and DR-107 generation-semantics joins, then name the reviewed condition-4 harness/owner for AL execution (or explicitly keep the affected DR-127 evidence at design standing). Do not borrow QUALIFIED or SATISFIED standing from DR-G16, DR-G21, or an unaccepted sibling.

verdictStatement: The control-race reference, source quotations, and non-authorizing posture are sound, but the anti-lockstep half is not an application-grade contract. It omits the pinned no-lockstep-version/no-same-version-coupling law, allowing a globally versioned bundle-gated promotion train, and its five labels have no reproducible fixture relation, oracle, evidence object, dependency activation, or execution owner. Preview scope matches live D-002 but is not sourced to it.

authorityOfThisVerdict.note: Independent measurement only. DR-127 remains OPEN; CC-1..CC-11 execution remains condition 4 / DR-G21 and supplies no DR-127 design-level SATISFIED standing.
